findings.summary: AC1 says the default image carries `pnpm`, but the code comment only claims `git` and `node/npm/corepack`. `node:22-bookworm` does not ship pnpm. Corepack has to download it, and the container runs with --network=none. In-container `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm test` will therefore likely fail for pnpm repos such as this one. The failure is fail-closed: it rejects and never falsely approves. But it can make the gate reject every pnpm-based PR. I did not run the image, so this is unverified. Either bake pnpm into the pinned image or confirm in the PR body how pnpm resolves offline.

findings.summary: The Stage 4 check reads only the two pass flags. It does not look at `sandboxError`, because that field is not part of the persisted report. This is safe today: `FAILURE_RESULT` sets both flags false. If another code path ever sets `sandboxError` without clearing the flags, Stage 4 would not catch it.

findings.summary: newTestsPassed comes from the exit code of the head test command, and the fork's package.json and tests decide that command. A hostile fork can force a pass (for example a `test` script of `exit 0`). Stage 4 now requires this flag, which only adds a check, so nothing is loosened. But the flag is not independent evidence; the reviewers remain the real control on head-side behaviour. Consider a code comment or doc note saying newTestsPassed is fork-influenced.

findings.summary: node:22-bookworm ships corepack but no pnpm binary. Under --network=none, `pnpm install ... || true` will fail quietly. The result fails closed (tests error, so the flags are false and the PR is rejected), so there is no security impact. It may block acceptance criterion 1 (image contains pnpm) and criterion 3 (Docker run against a fixture).
